units.function: HTTP compatibility tests ensuring the legacy member route still prevents Owner self-lockout and preserves custom permission grants after the granular-permissions upgrade.
units.dependencyDirection: Express access routes receive an authenticated board actor, validate a member patch, call AccessService, then persist CompanyMembership and PrincipalPermissionGrant state plus activity records.
units.keyDataModels: Board user actor, Company membership role/status, principal permission key with optional Project scope and granting user, and member PATCH response/error.
units.lifecycle: An Owner cannot demote themself through the role-only route; changing another member from admin to operator updates the role but retains an existing scoped task-assignment grant and its grantor provenance.
units.testAssessment: Two integration cases cover self-lockout and custom-grant preservation. Missing are actual authentication middleware, cross-Company IDs, non-owner actors, last-owner versus self distinction, status/archive changes, concurrent owner demotions, grant escalation after role downgrade, activity-log content, CSRF and transaction rollback. The fixture injects an Owner who is also instance admin, so route authorization separation is weakly exercised.
units.designRationale: Preserve safety and backward compatibility while moving from coarse roles to additive scoped grants, without silently erasing administrator-authored exceptions on a role-only update.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs stable human access administration through schema upgrades while preventing ownership lockout and retaining explicit, attributable exceptions.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the self/last-owner invariant and separation between role-only and role-plus-grant commands. Add optimistic versioning, authenticated actor/Company checks, immutable AccessDecision receipts and a post-change effective-permission diff. Role downgrade should flag grants that exceed the new role baseline for explicit confirmation rather than silently retain or erase them.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route preserves who granted the custom scope but does not require an accountable approver for the role/grant combination, nor prove that running Agent capabilities and sessions reflect the change. A demoted member may retain meaningful powers without a surfaced responsibility review.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for Company human membership lifecycle, last-Owner invariants, role-default/scoped permission grants, member archival and Work reassignment, instance access protection, compatibility backfill and membership copying during Company import.
units.dependencyDirection: AccessService mutates CompanyMembership, PrincipalPermissionGrant, InstanceUserRole and Issue assignment state; role-default helpers define baseline grants; a compatibility backfill derives memberships/grants from legacy human and Agent rows.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent principal membership and role/status, instance admin, permission key plus opaque scope/grantor, open versus terminal Issue assignee, Agent lifecycle status and compatibility/import counters.
units.lifecycle: The last active Owner cannot be demoted or suspended; archiving a member clears grants, reassigns open Work to a chosen human and returns it to todo while completed history keeps the original assignee; self, Owner/admin and instance-admin Company access receive removal protection; role defaults grant environment management only to Owner/admin; idempotent backfill adds missing human grants without replacing a custom scope and adds active memberships only for non-terminal Agents; import copies active humans with target role defaults.
units.testAssessment: Nine substantial integration cases cover last-owner safety, archival/history, protected access, role defaults, idempotent migration, Agent status filtering, import and scoped-grant preservation. Missing are multi-Owner concurrency and database locking, authorization of every service caller, SSO/HR deprovisioning, session/token/active-Run revocation, reassignment acceptance and responsibility contract, pending approvals, tasks with multiple roles, deny/expiry/conditions, separation of duties, grant versioning, immutable audit, import consent, duplicate identities and rollback across membership/grant/Issue updates. Agent membership is backfilled but effective Agent grants are not asserted.
units.designRationale: Preserve at least one administrator, soft-delete people to retain history, keep open work owned after offboarding, evolve roles into grants idempotently and avoid replacing explicit scoped policy during upgrades.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires first-class human employment/membership and accountable ownership lifecycle alongside Agents, with offboarding that preserves history but immediately removes authority and reassigns unfinished responsibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the last-owner invariant, archival-not-deletion, open-versus-historical Work treatment, grantor provenance, scoped-grant preservation and idempotent compatibility migration. Extend to IdentityPort/HR or enterprise directory binding, employment status, responsibility-contract transfer/acceptance, session/runtime/secret revocation, time-bound/conditional grants, separation-of-duties policy and immutable before/after audit. Company import must require explicit target-owner confirmation and map identities rather than automatically reproducing authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: Reassignment changes assignee and todo state but records no acceptance by the new accountable human or transfer evidence. Offboarding clears database grants without proving active tokens, Agent runs or external systems were revoked. Import can grant active target access from source membership without tested consent, and role defaults do not express legal/business accountability.

units.function: Minimal shared-schema tests for user profile image URLs and defaulting omitted combined member grants.
units.dependencyDirection: Server tests directly exercise shared Zod validators used by profile and combined membership/permission request routes.
units.keyDataModels: User display name/image URL and combined membershipRole/grants update payload.
units.lifecycle: HTTP(S) and Paperclip asset paths are accepted as profile images, data URIs are rejected, and omitted grants in a combined member update become an empty list.
units.testAssessment: Three narrow cases cover happy-path URLs, one dangerous URI family and default grants. Missing are javascript/file/ftp/protocol-relative URLs, exact asset path grammar, URL length/control characters, image-fetch SSRF behavior, Unicode names and the critical semantic distinction between an absent grants field and an explicitly empty list. Defaulting absence to [] can turn a partial update into grant deletion.
units.designRationale: Avoid large inline avatar payloads and normalize combined access-update inputs for simpler service code.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe profile resources and unambiguous patch semantics for high-impact access changes.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Use a managed AssetRef or tightly allowlisted HTTPS policy rather than arbitrary display URLs when servers fetch content. Preserve tri-state patch semantics: omitted grants means unchanged, explicit [] means revoke all, and replacement requires version/confirmation. Do not copy this combined-update default.
units.responsibilityConflict: A validator default can erase grants without the caller explicitly requesting revocation, obscuring intent and responsibility. Profile validation is unrelated to identity proof and does not bind an image asset to an authenticated person.
